reason: This passage from Exodus 2:16-21 depicts Moses intervening to help (יוֹשִׁעָן - yashua/rescued) the daughters of the Midianite priest who were being driven away (וַיְגָרְשׁוּם) by shepherds. The text emphasizes Moses' compassionate assistance—he rescues them and waters their flocks—but contains no explicit mention of violence. The passage demonstrates aid to those in need rather than establishing violence toward unruly people as a model of good leadership. The narrative's focus is on humanitarian intervention, not on force or violence as a governing principle.
